**UX owner:** [Jessica Thal](mailto:jfortun2@andrew.cmu.edu)  
**Dev lead:** [Darren Siegel](mailto:dmsiegel@andrew.cmu.edu)[Raphael Gachuhi](mailto:rgachuhi@andrew.cmu.edu)  
**Status:** Ready for review  
**Last updated:** 11/9/26  
**Jira epic:** [RMAP-110: Payments](https://eliterate.atlassian.net/browse/RMAP-110)  
**Figma:** [Figma](https://www.figma.com/design/6woKDEStD1bh70MJHqxNVw/Payments?node-id=144-6004&t=54Cvllva7aRLxD9t-1)  
**Prototype:** [https\://adminpayments.vercel.app/](https://adminpayments.vercel.app/) 

## **1\. Overview**

**Problem**

Creating and managing payment codes in Torus requires repetitive manual work and knowing which course template to look in. Administrators struggle to find individual codes, recover previously generated batches, and determine whether codes have been used. These gaps make routine distribution and student support slower and increase reliance on spreadsheets, workarounds, and staff with specialized knowledge.

**Intended outcome**

Give admins a clearer, more efficient way to create, find, and manage payment codes. Updated template-level designs support batch creation and downloads, while a centralized admin view lets staff locate batches and individual codes across templates, review their status, and take appropriate management actions. Together, these improvements should reduce manual work and help staff resolve code issues more confidently.

Enrollment reporting remains a separate follow-up pending stakeholder discussion and technical scoping.

## **3\. Shared Requirements**

* **Terminology:** Batch, Payment code, Deactivate/Reactivate  
* **Permissions:** Admin  
* **Accessibility:** All implementations should clearly label non-text content and be navigable by keyboard and screenreader. Note: we should be switching to “Title case” for buttons because that is how our new design system is intended and it is better for readability. 

## **⭐ Feature: Payment details on student profile** {#⭐-feature:-payment-details-on-student-profile}

**Figma frames / prototype:** [Figma](https://www.figma.com/design/6woKDEStD1bh70MJHqxNVw/Payments?node-id=144-9330&t=54Cvllva7aRLxD9t-1)  
**Readiness:** Ready for ticketing

### **User Need**

As an admin support team member, I need to see how a student paid for a specific course section so I can investigate payment issues and help resolve access problems.

### **Acceptance Criteria**

**Successful behavior**

* On a student’s profile page within a course section, **admins** can view a payment section containing:  
  * **Course fee:** The fee for the course section, formatted as currency.  
  * **Payment method:** The method associated with the student’s payment.  
  * **Payment reference, when available:**  
    * The payment code used.  
    * The CASHNet transaction reference for a card payment.  
    * Bypassed (when manually bypassed)  
* When the student has not paid, the payment method displays “Not paid.”  
* Update the page’s typography, spacing, colors, and components to match the design system and Figma specifications.

**Exceptions and safeguards**

* Display payment information for the selected student and course section.  
* Distinguish an unpaid enrollment from a payment bypass or a course with no fee.  
* If a payment exists but its reference is unavailable, display “Unavailable” while retaining the known payment method.  
* If payment information cannot be loaded, display an error message rather than showing the student as unpaid.  
* Display only the transaction reference for card payments; do not expose sensitive card information.

### **Accessibility Requirements**

* Use semantic headings and clearly associated labels and values.  
* Preserve readable content and logical reading order when zoomed or viewed on smaller screens.  
* If payment references are interactive, provide descriptive accessible names, keyboard access, and visible focus indicators.

### **Design Notes**

## **⭐ Feature: Global payment code interface** {#⭐-feature:-global-payment-code-interface}

**Figma frames / prototype:** [Figma](https://www.figma.com/design/6woKDEStD1bh70MJHqxNVw/Payments?node-id=144-6900&t=54Cvllva7aRLxD9t-1)  [https\://adminpayments.vercel.app/](https://adminpayments.vercel.app/) (navigate to Manage all Payment Codes)   
**Readiness:** Ready for ticketing

### **User Need**

As an admin managing payment codes, I need a central location to search codes across templates and download batches so I can find and manage codes without navigating to each template individually.

### **Acceptance Criteria**

**Successful behavior**

**Entry point**

* Add a “Manage all Payment Codes” link to the admin panel.  
* Selecting the link opens the central “Payment Codes” interface.  
* The interface displays all payment code batches across templates.  
* Existing codes without a batch are grouped under “Legacy Codes.”

**Batch table**

Display the following information for each batch:

| Column | Behavior |
| ----- | ----- |
| Batch name | Opens the batch and displays its codes. |
| Template | Displays the associated template and links to its Manage Payments page. |
| Cost | Displays the cost associated with the template. |
| Total codes | Displays the total number of codes in the batch. |
| Redeemed | Displays the number of redeemed codes. |
| Unused | Displays the number of unused codes. |
| Created | Displays the batch creation date. |
| Created by | Displays the admin recorded during batch creation. |
| Download | Downloads all codes in that batch with their associated information. |

**Search across batches**

* Support searching by batch name or payment code.  
* Searching for a payment code displays the batch containing the matching code.  
* When the admin opens that batch:  
  * Carry the payment code query into the batch’s search field.  
  * Display only matching codes.  
  * Visually highlight the matching code text.  
* Clearing the search restores the full list, subject to any active filters.

**Batch filters**

* Follow existing admin filter design patterns.  
* Support filtering by:  
  * Batch creation date range.  
  * Template, using a searchable selection control consistent with the institution filter.  
  * Created by.  
* Search and filters work together.  
* Display active filters and provide a “Clear all filters” action.

**Inside a batch**

* Display the batch name and associated template information.  
* Display each code’s:  
  * Payment code.  
  * Status: Unused, Redeemed, or Deactivated.  
  * Redeemed by: student name and redemption date, when applicable.  
  * Redeemed for: course section, when applicable.  
* Student names link to the student’s profile within the course section where the code was redeemed.  
* Course section names link to the section’s Manage page.  
* Support text search within the batch.  
* Support filtering by status: Unused, Redeemed, or Deactivated.  
* Search and status filters work together.  
* Provide navigation back to the central Payment Codes interface, preserving its search and filters 

**Downloads**

* Downloading from the central table exports the entire selected batch.  
* Downloading from inside a batch exports all matching results under the current search and filters, including results on other pages.  
* Include the payment code, status, associated template, batch information, and redemption information where available.

**Exceptions and safeguards**

* Restrict access and downloads to authorized admins.  
* Show an empty state when no batches exist.  
* When a search or filter returns no results, show a clear message and controls to revise or clear the criteria.  
* Validate date ranges and explain how to correct an invalid range.  
* Missing legacy metadata must not prevent codes from appearing or being downloaded. Display “Not available” where information cannot be recovered.  
* Leave redemption fields empty for codes that have not been redeemed.  
* Distinguish deactivated codes from unused codes; deactivated codes must not count as unused.  
* If a linked template, student profile, or course section is unavailable, retain the available information without presenting a broken link.  
* If loading or downloading fails, show an error with a retry action and preserve the current search and filters.  
* Searching, filtering, and downloading must not change code status or redemption information.

### **Accessibility Requirements**

* All links, search fields, filters, and download controls are keyboard accessible and have visible focus indicators.  
* Tables use semantic headers associated with their cells.  
* Search fields and filters have persistent, programmatically associated labels.  
* Row download controls have accessible names that identify the batch.  
* Search results, filter updates, empty states, and download errors are announced to assistive technology without moving focus unexpectedly.  
* Code highlighting is supplementary; matching results remain understandable without color.  
* Status labels use text and do not rely on color alone.  
* Date controls support keyboard entry and associate validation messages with the relevant field.  
* On entering a batch, focus moves to the batch heading. Returning to the batch list restores focus to the originating batch link.  
* At zoomed and narrow viewport sizes, all table information and actions remain accessible.

### **Design Notes**

## **⭐ Feature: Template code management** {#⭐-feature:-template-code-management}

**Figma frames / prototype:** [Figma](https://www.figma.com/design/6woKDEStD1bh70MJHqxNVw/Payments?node-id=144-6006&t=54Cvllva7aRLxD9t-1) [https\://adminpayments.vercel.app](https://adminpayments.vercel.app/) (toggle prototype to template, “manage payments”  
**Readiness:** Ready for ticketing

### **User Need**

As an admin, I need to search, review, and download payment code batches within a template so I can manage codes associated with that template.

### **Acceptance Criteria**

**Successful behavior**

* Update the template’s Manage Payments page to use the same batch table and interactions as the central Payment Codes interface, with the differences specified below.  
* Display description text: “Create and manage payment code batches for this template.”  
* Display only batches associated with the current template.  
* Group existing codes without a batch into a “Legacy Codes” batch for this template.

**Batch table**

* Include the same columns and behaviors as the central Payment Codes interface:  
  * Batch name, which opens the batch.  
  * Cost.  
  * Total codes.  
  * Redeemed codes.  
  * Unused codes.  
  * Creation date.  
  * Created by.  
  * Download batch.  
* Omit the Template column because the template is already established by the page context.

**Search and filters**

* Support the same batch-name and payment-code search behavior as the central interface, limited to the current template.  
* Searching for a payment code surfaces its containing batch.  
* Opening that batch preserves the code query, displays only matching codes, and highlights the matching code text.  
* Include only these batch filters:  
  * Creation date range.  
  * Created by.  
* Follow existing admin filter design patterns, display active filters, and provide “Clear all filters.”  
* Search and filters work together.

**Inside a batch and downloads**

* Use the same batch detail information, search, status filters, redemption links, and download behavior as the central interface.  
* Downloading from the batch table exports the entire selected batch.  
* Downloading from inside a batch exports all results matching the current search and filters, including results on other pages.  
* Returning to the template’s batch table preserves its search and filters.

**Exceptions and safeguards**

* Restrict access and downloads to authorized admins.  
* Search, filters, counts, and downloads must remain scoped to the current template.  
* Apply the same validation, missing-data handling, loading states, empty states, and error recovery as the central interface.  
* When no batches exist, display an empty state   
* When no results match, provide a clear message and controls to revise or clear the search and filters.  
* Searching, filtering, and downloading must not change code status or redemption information.

### **Accessibility Requirements**

* Apply the same accessibility requirements as the central Payment Codes interface, including:  
  * Keyboard access and visible focus indicators.  
  * Semantic table headers and labeled search and filter controls.  
  * Accessible download names identifying the associated batch.  
  * Announcements for results updates, empty states, and errors.  
  * Text-based status labels and search highlighting that does not rely on color alone.  
  * Accessible date validation.  
  * Focus management when entering and returning from a batch.  
  * Access to all information and actions at zoomed and narrow viewport sizes.

### **Design Notes**

## **⭐ Feature: Batch code creation**  {#⭐-feature:-batch-code-creation}

**Figma frames / prototype:** [Figma](https://www.figma.com/design/6woKDEStD1bh70MJHqxNVw/Payments?node-id=172-2481&t=54Cvllva7aRLxD9t-1) [Figma](https://www.figma.com/design/6woKDEStD1bh70MJHqxNVw/Payments?node-id=144-6007&t=54Cvllva7aRLxD9t-1)  
**Readiness:** Ready for ticketing

### **User Need**

As an admin, I need to generate up to 2,500 payment codes at once and name each batch so I can distribute large quantities of codes and organize them meaningfully.

### **Acceptance Criteria**

**Successful behavior**

* In the template’s Manage Payments page, display a primary “Create new batch” button.  
* Selecting the button opens a “Create new batch of payment codes” modal.  
* The modal includes:  
  * Helper text: “Create up to 2,500 codes in one batch.”  
  * A required “Number of codes” field.  
  * A required “Batch name” field that accepts free-form text without a prescribed naming format.  
  * A primary “Generate \[number\] codes” button that reflects the entered quantity.  
  * A “Cancel” button.  
* When the admin submits valid inputs:  
  * Generate the requested number of unique payment codes.  
  * Create a batch with the entered name and associate it with the current template.  
  * Record the creation date and the admin who created the batch.  
  * Show a loading state while generation is in progress.  
* After successful creation:  
  * Close the modal and show a success message identifying the batch and number of codes created.  
  * Display the batch in the template’s Manage Payments page and the central Payment Codes interface.

**Exceptions and safeguards**

* Restrict batch creation to authorized admins.  
* The number of codes must be a whole number between 1 and 2,500, inclusive.  
* Prevent submission and display an inline error for:  
  * A missing quantity: “Enter the number of codes to generate.”  
  * An invalid quantity: “Enter a whole number between 1 and 2,500.”  
  * A missing or whitespace-only batch name: “Enter a batch name.”  
* Duplicate batch names are allowed; each batch is stored as a distinct batch.  
* Preserve entered values when validation or generation fails.  
* Prevent repeated submissions while generation is in progress so repeated clicks do not create additional batches.  
* If generation fails, display a clear error and allow the admin to retry without creating duplicate codes or batches.  
* Do not report success unless the full requested quantity has been generated and saved.  
* Selecting “Cancel,” closing the modal, or pressing Escape before submission dismisses it without creating codes.

### **Accessibility Requirements**

* All controls are keyboard accessible and have visible focus indicators.  
* The modal has an accessible name associated with its title.  
* Opening the modal moves focus inside it; focus remains within the modal while it is open.  
* Closing the modal returns focus to “Create new batch.”  
* Both fields have persistent, programmatically associated labels; quantity guidance is associated with the quantity field.  
* Validation errors identify the affected field, explain how to correct it, and are announced to assistive technology.  
* On invalid submission, move focus to the first invalid field.  
* Loading, success, and failure messages are announced to assistive technology.  
* Errors and loading states do not rely on color alone.

### **Design Notes**

## **⭐ Feature: Deactivate/Reactivate Codes** {#⭐-feature:-deactivate/reactivate-codes}

**Figma frames / prototype:** [Figma](https://www.figma.com/design/6woKDEStD1bh70MJHqxNVw/Payments?node-id=144-6161&t=54Cvllva7aRLxD9t-1) [Figma](https://www.figma.com/design/6woKDEStD1bh70MJHqxNVw/Payments?node-id=144-6899&t=54Cvllva7aRLxD9t-1)  
**Readiness:** Ready for ticketing

### **User Need**

As an admin, I need to deactivate unused payment codes to prevent students from redeeming them and reactivate them when they should become available again.

### **Acceptance Criteria**

**Successful behavior**

* Within a batch, provide an action for each payment code based on its status:

| Code status | Action |
| ----- | ----- |
| Unused | Enabled “Deactivate” button |
| Redeemed | Disabled “Deactivate” button |
| Deactivated | Enabled “Reactivate” button |

**Deactivate a code**

* Selecting “Deactivate” opens a confirmation modal:  
  * Title: “Deactivate payment code?”  
  * Description: “Are you sure you want to deactivate this code? Once the code is deactivated, students can no longer redeem it. You can reactivate the code if necessary.”  
  * Display the affected payment code.  
  * Primary action: “Deactivate code.”  
  * Secondary action: “Cancel.”  
* Only after the admin selects “Deactivate code”:  
  * Change the code’s status to Deactivated.  
  * Prevent students from redeeming it.  
  * Replace the “Deactivate” action with “Reactivate.”  
  * Display a success message.  
  * Update batch counts and active filtered results in both template and central payment code management.

**Reactivate a code**

* Selecting “Reactivate” changes the code’s status to Unused and makes it available for redemption.  
* Replace the “Reactivate” action with “Deactivate.”  
* Display a success message and update batch counts and active filtered results.

**Exceptions and safeguards**

* Only authorized admins can deactivate or reactivate codes.  
* Redeemed codes cannot be deactivated. Provide an explanation alongside the disabled action: “Redeemed codes cannot be deactivated.”  
* Recheck the code’s status when confirming deactivation. If it has since been redeemed, prevent deactivation and explain why.  
* Selecting “Cancel,” closing the modal, or pressing Escape dismisses the confirmation without changing the code.  
* Prevent repeated submissions while an action is processing.  
* If an action fails, preserve the existing status and display an error with a retry option.  
* Deactivation and reactivation retain the same payment code and batch association.

### **Accessibility Requirements**

* All enabled actions are keyboard accessible and have visible focus indicators.  
* Action controls have accessible names identifying the affected code.  
* The confirmation modal has an accessible title and description.  
* Opening the modal moves focus to “Cancel”; focus remains within the modal until it closes.  
* Closing the modal returns focus to the originating action, or its replacement after a successful change.  
* The reason for a disabled action is available without hovering over or focusing the disabled button.  
* Status, success, and error messages are announced to assistive technology and do not rely on color alone.  
* If an updated code disappears from the active filtered results, move focus to a logical location and announce the result.

### **Design Notes**
